item.title: US Midterm Voters Deliver Brutal Verdict On Trump
item.description: Donald Trump faced a radically transformed and hostile political landscape on Wednesday after US voters handed control of Congress to the Democrats in a stunning rebuke to his presidency. The result was a personal humiliation for the 80-year-old Trump as a Democratic wave swept into his Republican heartland, boosted by anger at soaring energy costs and his costly, dragging war with Iran. The Democratic capture of both the Senate and the House of Representatives signals an end to Trump’s stranglehold on US politics and gives Democrats the power to block legislation, launch investigations into Trump’s administration and thwart his appointments. The results reflected deep frustration over the cost of living, tariffs and Trump’s war with Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. “This is so incredibly exciting. We can get our country back,” Kathy Jackoway said in Texas, celebrating a win by Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico. Trump struck a conciliatory tone despite his history of rejecting election defeats, telling The New York Times he was “absolutely willing” to accept the results. “I think the Democrats did a good job,” the 80-year-old told Fox News, in rare praise for his political opponents. “They fought hard.” Combo image of Democratic US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed (r) and President of the U.S Donald Trump (l) But he sought to distance himself from his party’s poor showing, adding: “I don’t view it as a hit on me.” He acknowledged that the Iran conflict had contributed to the result but defended the military campaign, and he suggested the rival parties could find common ground on immigration. Republican Heartland Democrats flipped seats that had long been held by Republicans, scoring breakthroughs in South Carolina, North Carolina, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Texas and Maine. In Maine, former logger Troy Jackson defeated longtime Republican Senator Susan Collins. In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton became the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932. Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008. In Texas, Democrats won not only a Senate seat but also the governor’s race, ending decades of Republican rule. Democrats protected key Senate seats of their own, including Jon Ossoff in Georgia and an open seat in New Hampshire. In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, making him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress. El-Sayed won despite a last-minute curveball when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, came out in support of Rogers. In the House, Democrats made gains in Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Arizona, North Carolina, Wisconsin and New Jersey, including districts Trump had carried comfortably in 2024. item.title: Police warn politicians against destroying campaign materials
item.description: …IGP orders commissioners to arrest, prosecute offenders By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigeria Police Force has warned politicians, political thugs and other individuals against the destruction or defacement of campaign posters, banners and billboards belonging to candidates and political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Force said offenders would be arrested and prosecuted, warning that political differences or loyalty to a particular party did not give anyone the right to destroy another candidate’s campaign materials. Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Iniedu, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday, saying the police had observed with concern growing incidents of deliberate tearing, defacement and destruction of campaign materials across the country. The statement read: “The Nigeria Police Force strongly condemns this act of political intolerance and warns political thugs, hoodlums and other mischief-makers involved to desist immediately. “For the avoidance of doubt, destroying, defacing or unlawfully removing another candidate’s campaign posters and billboards may constitute malicious damage, which is a criminal offence under applicable criminal laws, including Section 451 of the Criminal Code Act and Section 326 of the Penal Code Law, which defines the offence of mischief. “Political differences or loyalty to a particular party do not give anyone the right to destroy another candidate’s property or infringe on their right to campaign freely. “The Force reiterates that all political parties and candidates, irrespective of their affiliation or status, are entitled to equal protection under the law. “No individual or group has the right to determine whose campaign materials should be displayed or destroyed.” The police said the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, had directed commissioners of police in the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory to take proactive measures to prevent such incidents. He also directed them to investigate reported cases and ensure that anyone found culpable was arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law. The statement added that political sponsors and individuals who recruited, encouraged or facilitated the destruction of campaign materials would also be held accountable where evidence established their involvement. The Force urged political parties, candidates and their supporters to conduct their campaigns peacefully and respect the rights of others. It warned that political intolerance, intimidation and criminal conduct must not be allowed to undermine the democratic process. “The Nigeria Police Force will not allow political thugs and troublemakers to turn the nation’s political environment into a theatre of lawlessness. Those who choose to break the law will face the full consequences of their actions. “Be warned. Respect the law. Let democracy thrive,” the statement added. item.title: State Police Bill to reach Tinubu for assent today — Reps
item.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja ABUJA — The State Police Bill, seeking to decentralise policing responsibilities between the Federal and state governments, will be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday for assent. The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, disclosed this while presiding over plenary, following the approval of the proposed constitutional amendment by 29 of the 36 State Houses of Assembly. Kalu expressed excitement over the endorsement of the proposed police reform by more than two-thirds of the state legislatures, describing the development as a major step towards the establishment of state police in Nigeria. “The State Police Bill has received the backing of 29 State Assemblies. Later today, the Clerk to the National Assembly will transmit it to the President for assent,” he said. The approval by the state assemblies marks a significant milestone in efforts to amend the Constitution to allow states to establish and manage their own police forces alongside the Nigeria Police Force. The proposed reform is aimed at addressing concerns over Nigeria’s centralised policing structure, which critics argue limits the capacity of security agencies to respond effectively to local security challenges. Under the proposed arrangement, state governments would have greater responsibility for policing within their jurisdictions, while the Federal Government would retain its own police structure. The reform is expected to allow states to develop policing strategies tailored to their security needs, with the aim of strengthening intelligence gathering, community-based security and responses to crime. The transmission of the bill to the President marks the next stage in the constitutional amendment process, following its passage by the National Assembly and approval by the required number of state legislatures. The proposed establishment of state police has remained a major issue in Nigeria’s security reform debate, with supporters advocating decentralised policing as a means of improving security management across the country. item.title: UNICEF commends Taraba over education reforms
item.description: … As state launches Learning Passport in 50 pilot schools By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has commended the Taraba State Government for its education reforms, particularly the introduction of free and compulsory basic and secondary education, abolition of illegal school fees and distribution of free learning materials. The commendation was given by UNICEF Chief of Field Office, Bauchi, Dr Nuzhat Rafique, during the official launch of the Nigeria Learning Passport (NLP) in Jalingo. Rafique, who was represented by the Education Officer, UNICEF Bauchi Field Office, Raphael Aiyedipe, said the state’s education policies had contributed to an increase in school enrolment from approximately 760,000 to more than one million pupils since the inception of the current administration. She also applauded the government for promoting inclusive education for children with special needs, while strengthening teacher recruitment and professional development. According to her, the rollout of the digital learning platform was made possible through partnerships with Microsoft, the Global Partnership for Education (GPE), Airtel, IHS Towers and TECNO. She explained that the programme was designed to address connectivity barriers, reduce the number of out-of-school children and ensure continuity of learning, particularly in vulnerable communities. In his address, Governor Agbu Kefas reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to making education accessible to every child in the state, describing it as a cornerstone of sustainable development and national progress. Kefas, who was represented by the Head of Service, Dr Hamidu Kara, said the Nigeria Learning Passport represented a major step towards ensuring that no child was left behind in the state’s educational development. “The Nigerian Learning Passport represents a bold step forward in our commitment to ensure that no child is left behind in their educational journey, especially in these challenging times,” he said. He explained that the digital platform would provide flexible, accessible and inclusive learning opportunities, particularly for children affected by crises or disruptions to conventional schooling. The governor added that the initiative aligned with his administration’s free education agenda and urged stakeholders, teachers and students to embrace and promote the platform. Also speaking, the Commissioner for Secondary, Technical and Vocational Education, Dr Augustina Godwin, announced that the pilot phase of the programme would commence in 50 schools across the state. She assured that the government would expand the initiative to more schools to enable additional students to benefit from the digital learning platform. item.title: Voter Register: INEC to purge 1.5 million irregular registrants
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC is set to delete about 1.5 million voter registrations found to be irregular from the national register ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja while receiving a delegation on a courtesy visit to the Commission’s headquarters. The delegation was led by the Special Representative of the United Nations Secretary-General for West Africa and the Sahel and Head of the United Nations Office for West Africa and the Sahel (UNOWAS), Mr. Leonardo Santos Simão. Amupitan said technology-enabled verification helped the Commission isolate the affected entries. The deletions, he explained, are part of a comprehensive cleaning of the register through the claims and objections process. The final register is scheduled for publication on December 15, 2026. The INEC chairman said the Commission has registered approximately 103 million voters. Young Nigerians aged 18 to 34 make up nearly 29 per cent of them. He added that the distribution of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) is ongoing across the country. Amupitan said INEC would continue to strengthen the use of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) for accreditation, and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) for public access to polling-unit results. The Commission is also planning a mock accreditation and election exercise to test these tools, identify possible challenges and build public confidence before the 2027 polls. Amupitan identified misinformation, disinformation and foreign information manipulation as major threats to electoral integrity. He warned that the growing misuse of artificial intelligence and coordinated online campaigns could undermine public confidence in the electoral system. He therefore asked the UN for stronger collaboration on information integrity, countering electoral disinformation and public awareness. Other areas of prospective cooperation he outlined include conflict prevention, election security, early-warning mechanisms, stakeholder dialogue and peacebuilding. He also listed the protection of vulnerable groups, particularly women, youths and persons with disabilities. On security, Amupitan said INEC is working with relevant agencies to map areas vulnerable to electoral violence and other threats, so that preventive measures can be developed. Simão said the visit was meant to show UN support for INEC, noting that the Commission carries a significant responsibility in managing elections in a country confronted by terrorism and other security challenges. According to him, the UN will maintain a presence during the elections, not as observers since it has no mandate for election observation, but to encourage positive conduct and support an atmosphere conducive to peaceful participation. item.title: Kidnappers free six Benue mourners after N2.5m ransom
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The six mourners, including a bereaved man, who were abducted while conveying the corpse of his late wife from Kano State to Okpoga, headquarters of Okpokwu Local Government Area (LGA) of Benue State, have regained their freedom after spending several days in captivity. The victims were reportedly released by their abductors around 11pm on Tuesday after a ransom of N2.5 million was paid. A community member, Meddy Olotu, who disclosed this, said the kidnappers also demanded 10 plates of food as part of the conditions for releasing the victims. The six mourners, comprising the deceased woman’s husband and five other persons accompanying him, were kidnapped along Adoka Road in Otukpo LGA at about 8pm last Friday. They were reportedly transporting the woman’s corpse from Kano State to Okpoga for burial when they were intercepted by gunmen, who subsequently abandoned the corpse inside their vehicle. The abductors had initially demanded N15 million ransom for the release of the six victims. Confirming their release, Olotu said the victims regained their freedom after the ransom was paid and the food demand met. “They were released by their captors around 11pm Tuesday night after a ransom of N2.5 million was paid for their release. “Additionally, the captors also requested that when the ransom is being delivered, 10 plates of food should be brought to them. That was done and they have all regained their freedom,” he said. Olotu added that the victims were receiving medical attention after allegedly suffering torture and physical abuse while in captivity. “As I speak, they are receiving medical treatment because they were severely tortured and manhandled, so they need medical attention,” he said. The Chairman of Otukpo Local Government Area, Maxwell Ogiri, also confirmed the release of the abducted mourners on Tuesday night. However, efforts to reach the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, for confirmation and further details were unsuccessful, as he could not be reached at the time of filing this report. item.title: Photos: Atiku, Oyegun, Naja’atu, Dino Melaye arrive Sokoto for ADC campaign
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto Former Vice-President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has arrived at the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport, Sokoto, for the formal inauguration of his presidential campaign. Also arriving in Sokoto for the campaign flag-off were former National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), John Odigie-Oyegun; Hajiya Naja’atu Muhammad; and former Kogi West Senator, Dino Melaye. Naja’atu arrived in the company of the ADC presidential candidate, while the other political figures also joined the gathering ahead of the campaign inauguration. Atiku’s arrival attracted a large crowd of supporters and residents, many of whom gathered at the airport and along the route to catch a glimpse of the opposition candidate. The large turnout is expected to delay his arrival at the campaign venue, as supporters lined up to welcome him. Earlier, some youths identified as supporters of the APC reportedly attempted to block roads leading to the venue. However, they were reportedly overwhelmed by the large crowd, allowing movement towards the venue to continue. item.title: Don’t politicise national security, TMS warns Atiku as DSS probes Sokoto protest
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation otherwise known as Tinubu Must Stay TMS has warned former Vice President Atiku Abubakar against politicising national security, as the Department of State Services DSS investigates his allegation that it mobilised protesters to disrupt campaign activities in Sokoto State. Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC, made the accusation against the DSS. The agency denied it, but said its Director General had ordered an investigation. In a statement signed by TMS’ Director of Strategic Communication, Adebisi Adams, the group said claims involving security institutions must be backed by proof and tested through an impartial inquiry. TMS Director General, Marcel Ngogbehei, acknowledged the right of political leaders to scrutinise public institutions and demand accountability. He cautioned, however, against dragging sensitive security matters into partisan contests through allegations that have not been substantiated. “These are serious accusations. They deserve credible evidence, due process and an impartial investigation,” Ngogbehei said. According to him, national security should not be reduced to an instrument of partisan advantage. He said Atiku, as a former Vice President and prominent national figure, should appreciate the potential consequences of grave allegations against institutions entrusted with protecting lives and maintaining national security. TMS drew attention to the DSS account of an incident involving the Sokoto ADC governorship candidate, Mannir Daniya, on 31 October 2026. According to the DSS, its operatives evacuated Daniya to safety after he came under attack, while two of its personnel were assaulted and required hospital treatment. The DSS added that Daniya later contacted its Sokoto State Director to express appreciation and ask for additional reinforcement. TMS said that account, if established by the investigation, raises important questions that must be reconciled with the allegation that the same agency was organising disruption against the opposition. “Our security agencies carry the enormous responsibility of protecting Nigerians, maintaining public order and safeguarding democratic activities, regardless of political affiliation. Their professionalism, independence and credibility must not become casualties of political competition,” Ngogbehei said. The TMS Director General welcomed the DSS’ decision to investigate and urged Atiku to submit any evidence available to him and cooperate with the appropriate authorities. He also called on the DSS to ensure that its investigation is thorough and impartial, and that any misconduct established through due process attracts appropriate accountability. “Let there be no misunderstanding: defending the integrity of our security institutions does not mean placing them above scrutiny. item.title: Emami to Tinubu: Don’t succumb to blackmail, accuses INEC of flouting President’s intervention on delineation
item.description: Itsekiri leader, Chief Ayirimi Emami, has called on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu not to succumb to blackmail, regarding the unending controversy surrounding delineation of units and wards in Warri Federal Constituency. Emami, who was irked by the latest upload of units and wards by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC on its portal, as it relates to Warri South Local Government Area, stated that the Chairman of INEC, Professor Joash Ojo Amupitan, the Senate President, Godswill Obot Akpabio and some ethnic bigots, were trying to blackmail President Tinubu, to backtrack on his intervention regarding the controversial delineation of units and wards in Warri Federal Constituency, particularly as it affects Warri South Local Government Area. The APC Chieftain and Ologbotsere of Warri Kingdom, asserted that President Tinubu, during a peace meeting he convened at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, on June 11, 2026, emphatically stated that there was need to change the nomenclature of the three controversial wards proposed by INEC in the GRA, Pessu and Dore Market axis of Warri South Local Government Area. Emami, in a statement made available to newsmen, Wednesday November 4, said President Tinubu, had in the meeting attended by Delta State Governor, Rt. Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori, the National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, seven representatives each from Itsekiri, Ijaw and Urhobo ethnic Nationalities, charged Itsekiris, Ijaws and Urhobos in Warri Federal Constituency to live together in brotherhood and encouraged mutual respect. President Tinubu, reportedly told the ethnic leaders in attendance, that he saw the units and wards delineation proposal for Warri South – West Local Government Area, as the major contention, hence he proposed 11/9 solution for Ijaws and Itsekiris in the local government area. The President, posited that a separate state constituency for Ijaws in Warri South – West and Warri North Local Government Areas, with Itsekiris having state constituencies of their own in the two local government areas, should address any fear of ethnic deprivation in terms of political representation in the State House of Assembly. item.title: Delta seeks patience over N4bn poverty fund disbursement
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi ASABA — The Delta State Government has appealed to residents to exercise patience over the disbursement of its N4 billion poverty alleviation fund, assuring that 15,000 indigent beneficiaries across the state’s 25 local government areas would be covered. The General Manager of the Delta State Social Investment Programme (DSSIP), Chief Henry Sakpra, gave the assurance in Asaba, saying necessary arrangements had been concluded to ensure a smooth, transparent and hitch-free disbursement. “We urge Deltans to be patient as the necessary modalities have been put in place to ensure hitch-free, seamless disbursement,” Sakpra said. He assured that the N4 billion earmarked for the intervention would be judiciously utilised to support vulnerable residents, stressing that the programme was not designed to serve the interests of individuals seeking to exploit the initiative. According to him, the government is committed to ensuring that the funds reach genuine beneficiaries through a transparent and accountable process. Sakpra said due process would be followed in identifying beneficiaries and implementing the scheme to prevent diversion of funds and ensure that the intervention achieves its intended objectives. He explained that the programme was designed to alleviate poverty, empower vulnerable residents and improve their living conditions through targeted government support. “The focus is to provide meaningful support to vulnerable Deltans who genuinely require government intervention rather than allow the funds to be diverted from their intended purpose,” he said. The DSSIP boss also said the programme would be sustained as long as it continued to address the needs and aspirations of residents. “The programme would continue to run as long as Deltans are satisfied with it, as long as the programme satisfies the yearnings and the needs of Deltans,” he stated. The N4 billion intervention is expected to benefit 15,000 indigent persons across the state’s 25 local government areas. The initiative is part of the state government’s social investment drive under Governor Sheriff Oborevwori’s MORE Agenda, which prioritises poverty reduction, inclusive development and improved welfare. Sakpra reaffirmed the government’s commitment to people-oriented initiatives, saying the DSSIP would continue to implement programmes aimed at improving livelihoods and extending support to vulnerable communities across the state. item.title: Oyebanji seeks FG support for livestock development
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has sought increased Federal Government support and collaboration to expand livestock development, create jobs and boost economic opportunities in the state. Oyebanji made the appeal on Tuesday while receiving the Minister of Livestock Development, Idi Mukhtar Maiha, who was in the state to commission an ultra-modern veterinary hospital in Ado-Ekiti and inspect ongoing projects under the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (LPRESS) programme. The governor said livestock development had enormous potential to improve agricultural productivity, generate wealth, create employment and strengthen livelihoods. He called for stronger collaboration between the state and the Federal Government to harness opportunities in the sector, particularly through interventions aimed at improving livestock production and developing its value chain. Oyebanji commended President Bola Tinubu for establishing a separate Ministry of Livestock Development, describing agriculture and livestock as critical sectors for job creation and economic growth. He said his administration was committed to working with the Federal Government, investors and other stakeholders to unlock the sector’s potential and position Ekiti as an attractive destination for livestock investment. The governor urged the minister to assess the state’s ongoing projects, particularly the Ikun Dairy Farm, where he said federal intervention was needed to expand operations and improve sustainability. “I don’t believe in noise making; I believe the only way to advertise yourself is by showcasing your achievements,” he said. He added that the state had reached a stage where additional Federal Government support was necessary to enable its livestock initiatives to achieve greater impact. Earlier, Maiha commended Oyebanji for prioritising agriculture as a means of tackling poverty and unemployment, creating wealth and expanding economic opportunities. The minister assured the governor of the Federal Government’s readiness to strengthen its partnership with Ekiti to expand the agricultural value chain, increase production and sustain the state’s efforts towards food security. Maiha said his working visit included the commissioning of the veterinary hospital and inspection of LPRESS projects across the state. The facilities scheduled for inspection included the Ikun Dairy Farm, Emure Poultry Hub, cattle market in Ado-Ekiti, the ongoing construction of a semi-automated abattoir and the Erifun Broiler Processing Plant in Ado-Ekiti, among others. Also present at the meeting were the Chief of Staff, Niyi Adebayo; Special Adviser on Agriculture and Food Security, Ebenezer Boluwade; Special Adviser on Media, Yinka Oyebode; and LPRESS State Coordinator, Olayinka Adedipe. item.title: Ilhan Omar wins fifth US Congress term despite Trump attacks
item.description: Democratic Congresswoman Ilhan Omar has won a fifth term in the United States House of Representatives, retaining her seat for Minnesota’s 5th Congressional District despite criticism from President Donald Trump and an ongoing federal investigation. Omar defeated Republican candidate John Nagel in Tuesday’s midterm elections, according to projections by CBS News. The Somali-born lawmaker has been a vocal critic of Trump and has repeatedly faced attacks from the president over her background and political views. Her re-election comes amid a federal investigation involving allegations concerning her immigration and naturalisation records. On October 12, federal agents searched Omar’s Washington, DC, residence as part of the investigation. Her phone and passport were reportedly seized, while subpoenas were issued to some of her relatives. Trump had called on the congresswoman to resign, renewing allegations of identity fraud after a court filing identified her by an additional name. Omar has consistently denied any wrongdoing and has not been charged with a crime. Former US President Barack Obama has accused Trump of targeting the Minnesota lawmaker because of her political views. Omar has represented Minnesota’s 5th Congressional District since 2019, after winning the 2018 midterm elections. She was among the first two Muslim women elected to the US House of Representatives. In her victory speech, Omar said her re-election demonstrated that voters would support candidates who prioritised compassion and empathy in their leadership. item.title: Plateau PDP Chieftain Zang rejects APC campaign council appointment
item.description: …Reaffirms loyalty to party By Golok Nanmwa, Jos A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Plateau State, Hon. Aminu Zang, has rejected his inclusion in the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 Presidential and Governorship Campaign Council in the state, insisting that he remains a committed member of the opposition party. Zang, whose name reportedly appeared as number 254 on the published list of the APC Campaign Council’s Central Planning Committee, said he was neither consulted nor informed before his name was included in the committee. In a statement titled “Clarification on My Inclusion in the 2027 Plateau State Presidential and Governorship Campaign Council – Central Planning Committee (CPC)”, Zang said his political allegiance remained firmly with the PDP and the Rainbow Coalition. He said, “While I sincerely appreciate those who considered me worthy of inclusion and deemed me suitable for the responsibilities associated with this important assignment, I wish to state, unequivocally and without any ambiguity, that I remain an unrepentant and committed member of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) of the RAINBOW COALITION extraction.” Speaking in a telephone conversation with our correspondent, Zang said, “They didn’t consult me. I’m not angry, so to speak. “But, like, if you read the statement that I issued, I thanked those who felt that I was worthy of inclusion in the campaign council list.” He added, “Unfortunately for them, I am a bona fide member of the PDP, so I cannot belong to the PDP and now be in the APC campaign council team. I cannot.” On his political position ahead of the 2027 general elections, Zang said, “I am supporting Wike’s position that Tinubu returns, but for the governor, no way. I’m in the PDP.” He further declared, “Of course, we have a candidate in the PDP, Chief Kefas Wungak Ropshik.” He also disclosed that the PDP had yet to constitute its campaign council, saying, “No, not yet. They are working on it.” In his statement, Zang urged political stakeholders, party members, supporters and members of the public to embrace peace, tolerance, civility and political decorum ahead of the 2027 general elections. He said, “The electoral process should be approached with maturity, mutual respect and a strong sense of responsibility.” He also urged all stakeholders to seek the guidance and intervention of Almighty God for a peaceful electoral process. item.title: Trump rout a ‘new era’, could reset ties – S/Africa president
item.description: President Cyril Ramaphosa said Wednesday the Democrats’ rout of the Republicans in US midterm elections heralded a “new era in world relations” and could thaw strained ties between Pretoria and Washington. US-South Africa tensions have mounted over a range of policy disputes, culminating in Washington’s removal this week of South Africa from a trade deal offering eligible sub-Saharan African countries preferential US market access. “I do think that this group is going to introduce a new era in world relations,” Ramaphosa told reporters when asked about the Democratic result. “We’re hoping that on a bilateral basis, there will be a coming together of minds where we will find a proper path forward on geopolitics as well as on trade matters and investment matters,” Ramaphosa said, speaking after voting in local government elections. The US decision to exclude South Africa as well as Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) is set to take effect on January 1, with fears it could cost the battered local economy thousands of jobs. South Africa is the biggest beneficiary of the programme. The two countries have clashed over race, trade and diplomacy, with Washington cutting aid, imposing tariffs, expelling South Africa’s ambassador and boycotting a G20 summit in Johannesburg, against the backdrop of the country’s unresolved legacy of white minority rule. Last year, President Donald Trump berated Ramaphosa in the Oval Office over discredited claims of a “white genocide”. South Africa — Africa’s most industrialised nation — is the United States’ largest trading partner on the African continent, with more than 500 US businesses and 30,000 US citizens based in the country. item.title: Real Madrid to appoint tennis legend Rafa Nadal to board
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Real Madrid are set to appoint tennis great Rafael Nadal to their Board of Directors after the 22-time Grand Slam champion accepted an invitation from club president Florentino Perez to join its leadership. The Spanish club announced on Wednesday that Nadal’s appointment would be presented to representative members for ratification at an Extraordinary General Assembly scheduled for Saturday, November 21. According to Marca, the proposal was unanimously approved by the club’s Board of Directors and will be submitted in line with Article 46 of Real Madrid’s statutes. Nadal, 40, confirmed his acceptance in a message on X, thanking Perez and the board for the invitation and expressing his enthusiasm about taking up the new responsibility. “I want to thank President Florentino Perez and the Board for inviting me to become a member of Real Madrid’s Board of Directors,” he wrote. “I have accepted this proposal with great enthusiasm, eager to learn and to contribute in any way I can.” Real Madrid also praised the former world number one, describing him as a figure of immense sporting and human stature and a benchmark in Spanish and world sport. The club said it was a source of pride to have Nadal join its board and contribute to its present and future. The appointment will be considered at the Extraordinary General Assembly at the basketball pavilion of Ciudad Real Madrid, where the club’s Ordinary and Extraordinary General Assemblies will hold both in-person and online sessions. Nadal has maintained a close relationship with Real Madrid for years and has been an honorary club member since 2011. His appointment is also likely to renew speculation about a possible future role as club president, although he has not announced any such ambition as part of the latest development. In 2023, the former tennis star admitted that becoming Real Madrid president was an appealing idea but said he would first have to assess whether he was capable of taking on the responsibility. He also distanced himself from reports that he would contest the club’s presidential election earlier this year, which Perez won in June. Nadal retired from professional tennis in 2024 after a remarkable career that included 22 Grand Slam singles titles, among them a record 14 French Open crowns. item.title: PHOTOS: Preparations Ongoing for ADC Presidential Campaign Kick-off
item.description: Preparations are ongoing at the African Democratic Congress (ADC) secretariat in Sokoto, doubling as the venue of the ADC presidential campaign flag-off. The venue is being prepared ahead of the event, while supporters and party members are expected to gather for the campaign. The situation is currently calm.
